key_insight: Mesh4D compresses an entire animation sequence into a single compact latent code via a feed‑forward autoencoder guided by skeletal priors, enabling one‑pass monocular reconstruction of complete 3D shape and temporal motion as a deformation field.
problem_solved: Reconstructing and tracking a dynamic object's full 3D geometry and motion (4D mesh) from a single monocular video without multi‑view data or costly per-sequence optimization.
method: Feed‑forward autoencoder that maps an input monocular video to a compact latent representation encoding the whole animation.
Decoder predicts a deformation field and per‑frame meshes to produce complete 3D shape and motion in a single pass.
Training is guided by object skeletal structure to impose strong priors on plausible deformations and improve temporal coherence.
impact: Delivers fast, scalable 4D mesh reconstruction and tracking from single‑camera footage, lowering barriers for animation, AR/VR, and dynamic scene understanding by reducing dependence on multi‑view setups and slow optimization pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input monocular frames → single latent code → decoder → per‑frame 3D meshes (animated sequence).
Before/after comparison: monocular input vs reconstructed 4D mesh animation (overlayed frames).
Skeletal prior visualization: skeleton guiding deformation fields over mesh (arrows/warps).
Bar chart/table comparing runtime and accuracy against multi‑view or optimization‑based baselines.
paper_title: Mesh4D: 4D Mesh Reconstruction and Tracking from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Zeren Jiang, Chuanxia Zheng, Iro Laina, Diane Larlus, Andrea Vedaldi
